question:
A 57-year-old male seeks emergency care in New Mexico, reporting dyspnea and dry cough for the
past 12 hours. One week prior, he experienced a self-limited episode of fever, chills, fatigue, and
muscle aches lasting 3 days, which he dismissed as a common cold. After feeling well for several days,
he developed shortness of breath that occurs even without exertion. His occupation as an exterminator
recently involved work in a house with significant rodent infestation. On examination, he appears thin
and tachypneic with bilateral rales throughout his lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely
cause of his condition? Answer Choices: (A) Elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (B) Elevated
inflammatory markers with eosinophilia (C) Ground-glass opacities on chest CT (D) Widened
mediastinum on chest radiograph (E) Presence of Sin Nombre virus antibodies (F) Binding to sialic acid
residues in human cells (G) Safety pin-shaped organisms on peripheral blood smear (H) Diffuse
alveolar hemorrhage pattern (I) Decreased serum albumin level (J) Increased capillary permeability
 A. Presence of Sin Nombre virus antibodies
B. Binding to sialic acid residues in human cells
C. Safety pin-shaped organisms on peripheral blood smear
D. Increased capillary permeability
E. Ground-glass opacities on chest CT
F. Decreased serum albumin level
G. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage pattern
H. Elevated pulmonary vascular resistance
I. Widened mediastinum on chest radiograph

J. Elevated inflammatory markers with eosinophilia
